title: Let All the Earth Their Voices Raise
description: Let All the Earth Their Voices Raise in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 295 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"The Gentiles shall see thy Righteousness."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let all the earth their voi-ces raise, To sing the choic-est psalm of praise; To sing and bless Je-ho-vah's name: His glo-ry let the hea-then know, His won-ders to the na-tions show, And all his sa-ving works pro-claim.

lines: Let all the earth their voices raise,
To sing the choicest psalm of praise;
To sing and bless Jehovah's name:
His glory let the heathen know,
His wonders to the nations show,
And all his saving works proclaim.
The heathen know thy glory, Lord:
The wondering nations read thy word:
Our worship shall no more be paid
To gods which mortal hands have made;
Our Maker is our God alone.
Come the great day, the glorious hour,
When earth shall feel his saving power,
And barbarous nations fear his name;
Then shall the race of man confess
And in his courts his grace proclaim.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
